extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer-algebra system (mathematicians/programmers writing Magma code)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and operational rules for writing and running Magma sessions, scripts, I/O, formatted printing, file and process interaction, editing, timing, and environment settings. Intended to inform correct usage and good practice when producing Magma code and controlling Magma sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbose printing flags
rubrics_metrics.description: For some of the major algorithms in Magma, it is possible to request that information on the progress of the algorithm be provided during execution. By default, all the flags for verbose printing are turned off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SetVerbose(s, x) to set a verbosity flag named by string s and GetVerbose(s) to query it. For flags with only two settings, use 0/false for 'off' and 1/true for 'on'. For multi-level flags, 0/false is 'off', small positive integers denote increasing verbosity levels, and true denotes the minimum non-zero verbosity level. Examples of flag names include "OnanScott" and "Conj".

rubrics_metrics.name: User spare verbosity flags
rubrics_metrics.description: There are five spare flags available for use in user-defined intrinsics or functions/procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their names are "User1", ..., "User5" and their possible settings are 0/false ('off', the default) and 1/true ('on').

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatted printing with printf
rubrics_metrics.description: The printf-statement prints a format string with values substituted for placeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: printf format_string, expr, ..., expr; The format string must contain %o and/or %m the same number of times as there are expressions. The format string may be any expression returning a string. %o prints in "Default" printing mode; %m prints in "Magma" printing mode. Use printf for greater control than comma-separated print. The printf-statement can be used across several calls to build one output line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printf newline behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If a newline is desired at the end of a printf output, the format string must include \n; otherwise no newline will occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows building an output line gradually from several printf-statements. However, Magma will flush the buffer and perform a newline before giving the prompt if a prompt is imminent and output is waiting. Still, it is good practice to supply the newline explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between %o and %m
rubrics_metrics.description: %o stands for 'object' (Default printing mode) and %m stands for 'magma' (Magma printing mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values corresponding to %o are printed in "Default" printing mode whereas values for %m are printed in "Magma" mode. Use %m when you want Magma-style terse identifiers (e.g., Sym(3) /* order = 6 = 2 * 3 */) and %o for fuller descriptive output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use printf with tabs/newlines for tabulated output
rubrics_metrics.description: The printf-statement is often used with tab and newline characters for tabulated output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine %o/%m placeholders with \t and \n and multiple printf calls to construct formatted tables. See other examples in the manual (e.g., tabulated output examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: read statement for string input
rubrics_metrics.description: read identifier; causes Magma to pause waiting for user-typed input; identifier gets the typed string (empty string if nothing typed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the form read identifier, string; which prints the provided prompting string before reading. Prompting phrases should be worded to make the intention clear to the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: readi statement for integer input
rubrics_metrics.description: readi identifier; is designed for integer input; the input must be a representation of a literal integer (an integer-string).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use readi ident, "prompt" to prompt. The typed line must conform to the integer-string format as defined elsewhere in the manual. Example: readi age, "What is your age (in years)?"

rubrics_metrics.name: Load statement usage during a session
rubrics_metrics.description: load F ; reads the contents of file F into Magma as if entered at the keyboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F may be a full pathname or pathname relative to current directory. If relative, Magma tries current directory, then MAGMA_PATH directories, then libraries/databases. An error is given if all attempts fail. The load-statement must appear at top level (not inside other constructions) because load is a parser instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAGMA_PATH and GetPath/SetPath
rubrics_metrics.description: MAGMA_PATH is a colon-separated list of directories used by Magma to search for files when relative pathnames are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GetPath() returns MAGMA_PATH as a string, and SetPath(P) changes it for the current Magma session. Issues with environment variables are OS tasks and may require local assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning identifiers at start-up
rubrics_metrics.description: On the command line, after 'magma' you may supply filename arguments and ident:=string assignments to set identifier values at start-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only literal strings may be assigned at start-up. Syntax is ident:=string with no spaces around := and no terminating semicolon. Place assignments after the magma command interspersed with filenames; assignments happen in the order given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using a standard start-up file
rubrics_metrics.description: If MAGMA_STARTUP_FILE environment variable points to a file, it will be loaded automatically at start-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The start-up file typically contains abbreviations, assignments, and environment settings to customize the system. Use 'magma -n' to start Magma without loading the usual start-up file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Echoing contents of loaded files
rubrics_metrics.description: SetEchoInput(v) requests that contents of files loaded into Magma be echoed on screen or to output/log files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is no echoing. SetEchoInput(true) makes subsequent loaded files have their contents echoed. GetEchoInput() returns current setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending output to an output file or log file
rubrics_metrics.description: SetOutputFile(F) directs Magma's output to file F; SetLogFile(F) creates a log file recording both input and output from that time onward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use UnsetOutputFile()/UnsetLogFile() to stop. There cannot be more than one output or log file in operation simultaneously—setting a second file stops sending data to the first. By default Magma appends to existing files; set Overwrite=true to truncate and write afresh. HasOutputFile() returns true and the filename if a file is defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read whole file into string
rubrics_metrics.description: Read(F) returns the contents of file F as a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard string operations may then be used to analyze this string in Magma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write/PrintFile to write formatted output to files
rubrics_metrics.description: Write(F, x, L) or PrintFile(F, x, L) writes the string that would be produced by printing x at level L to file F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sprint(x, L) constructs the string without writing. If "Default" level is desired, use Write(F,x) or PrintFile(F,x); for "Magma" level use PrintFileMagma(F,x). Overwrite parameter behaves like SetOutputFile/SetLogFile.

rubrics_metrics.name: File-object operations for partial I/O
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Open(F, t) to get a File object for reading/writing; manipulate with Put, Puts, Gets, Getc, Ungetc, IsEof, Rewind, Tell, Seek, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Gets or Getc test the result with IsEof to check for EOF marker before using it. When file is no longer required, delete its identifier or reassign it so Magma will close the file (unless multiple references exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type indicator strings for Open/POpen
rubrics_metrics.description: The type indicator t in Open and POpen should be a string using the same values as C fopen()/popen() for your OS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common values: "r", "w", "a", "r+", "w+", "a+". On PC include "b" for binary mode. For POpen only "r" and "w" are meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check EOF when reading in a loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern: s := Gets(f); while not IsEof(s) do ... s := Gets(f); end while;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always test Gets/Getc results with IsEof before using; example provided for reading a spelling list file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appending vs overwriting files when writing
rubrics_metrics.description: By default Magma appends to existing files when writing; Overwrite parameter set to true causes truncate-and-write behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Overwrite=true in SetOutputFile/SetLogFile/PrintFile/Write if you want to discard old contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving and restoring workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: save F ; quit; and later restore F ; will save and restore the workspace (identifiers, structural info, environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unwise to restore a workspace in the midst of a session because the current workspace will be destroyed. Delete irrelevant values before saving to reduce memory usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: System calls and shell escape
rubrics_metrics.description: System(s) calls an operating-system process; %!c executes shell command c outside Magma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System may be used as a function returning the command's return value for error-checking. Shell-escape output resembles System but is not recorded in Magma history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipe(C, s) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Pipe(C, s) creates a pipe to shell command C, sends s into C's stdin, and returns C's output as a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For many commands, s should finish with a newline if it is only one line. Use Regexp on the returned string to extract values if needed (example with GP/Pari).

rubrics_metrics.name: POpen(C, t) pipes
rubrics_metrics.description: POpen(C, t) opens a pipe between Magma and shell command C (ending with newline) and returns a Magma file object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type indicator t is "r" (read) or "w" (write); the file object may be manipulated with file functions (Puts, Gets, etc.). Example: using POpen with grep to write matching lines to an output file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary names and process id
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempname(s) returns a unique string beginning with s (using mktemp), and Getpid() returns the current Magma process ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Tempname to create unique temporary filenames when multiple Magma processes might create files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab completion behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Tab completion minimizes typing by completing intrinsics, identifiers, and reserved words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pressing Tab completes as far as possible; pressing again lists all possible completions. A beep warns when ambiguous. Behavior is best learned experimentally; examples in manual show completing names like QuadraticField and AbsolutePrecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line editing keys and modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma provides a line editor with control-character shortcuts; Emacs-mode is default with optional VI mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use control-a/e/f/b etc. as listed in Table 15.1. Change to VI bindings with SetViMode(true). The control characters work in both modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: History usage and editing previous lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma stores the last 50 lines of input by default (SetHistorySize/GetHistorySize to change) and provides % commands to print, repeat, and edit history lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use %p to print history, %n (number) to repeat, %n1 n2 to repeat ranges, and %e (line number) to edit a previous line in an external editor defined by EDITOR environment variable (or /bin/ed). Control-p/control-n can recall previous lines interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupting or forcing a stop
rubrics_metrics.description: Typing control-c during execution performs an interrupt; typing control-c twice quickly (within half a second) forces Magma to stop (exit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single control-c to interrupt long computations to try alternative approaches. Use double control-c only as a last resort since it exits the whole Magma system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing Magma operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix a statement with time to execute it and print the CPU seconds used. Use Cputime() to time groups of statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: time n := 123456^987; For multiple statements: t := Cputime(); ... print Cputime(t); Cputime() returns time since session start; Cputime(t) returns time since t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrolling long output (SetRows)
rubrics_metrics.description: SetRows(n) restricts output to a maximum of n rows at a time; when output exceeds n rows the user is prompted to continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SetRows(0) turns off the output filter. Example: SetRows(20) will show 20 rows then 'Press return for more'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory limit settings
rubrics_metrics.description: SetMemoryLimit(n) or the environment variable MAGMA_MEMORY_LIMIT can impose a soft limit (in bytes) on memory allocated to Magma; default is no soft limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GetMemoryLimit() returns the current setting; a value of zero denotes no soft limit. Set a soft limit to avoid excessive swap usage on shared machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of reserved words and operator precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma has a set of reserved words and defined operator precedence which affect parsing and meaning of code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the reserved words list (e.g., do, if, else, intrinsic, printf, etc.) and the Precedence of Operators table when writing code to avoid name collisions and parse surprises.
